answerFirstFaq.question: What is a protective award under UK employment law?
answerFirstFaq.answer: A protective award is compensation of up to 90 days gross pay ordered by an Employment Tribunal under Section 189 of TULRCA 1992 when an employer fails to follow collective redundancy consultation rules. It is paid in addition to statutory redundancy and notice pay. Employers customarily contribute toward independent solicitor advice.

schemaSpecification.targetFaqQuestion: How is a settlement agreement taxed under UK employment law?

copyPackage.calibratedMetaDescription: Calculate tax on your UK settlement agreement. See your £30,000 statutory tax exemption (ITEPA 2003). Free check. SRA solicitor advice contribution.

answerFirstFaq.question: How is a settlement agreement taxed under UK employment law?
answerFirstFaq.answer: Under Section 403 of ITEPA 2003, genuine compensation payments up to £30,000 are completely tax-free. Any contractual earnings, accrued holiday pay, or payment in lieu of notice (PILON under PENP rules) remain subject to normal income tax and National Insurance. Employers customarily contribute toward independent legal advice.
